gloss: allotted time; time available to a player or speaker

definitions.gloss: allotted time; one's own share of time
definitions.explanation: The amount of time assigned to one side or one person — a player's clock in shogi, go, or chess, or the minutes given to a speaker or presenter. Once it runs out, the turn or the talk is over.

examples.japanese: {持|も}ち{時間|じかん}は{十分|じゅっぷん}です。
{持|も}ち{時間|じかん}が{残|のこ}り{少|すく}なくなってきた。
examples.english: There is not much time left on my clock.

examples.japanese: この{対局|たいきょく}は{持|も}ち{時間|じかん}が{各|かく}{三時間|さんじかん}で、{使|つか}い{切|き}ると{一手|いって}{一分|いっぷん}で{指|さ}さなければならない。
examples.english: Each player has three hours in this match, and once that is used up they must move within one minute per move.

notes:
{持|も}つ (to hold) plus {時間|じかん} (time): the time one "holds" and may spend as one likes. Standard vocabulary in board games and in conference or debate programs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {持|も}ち{時間|じかん}を{使|つか}い{切|き}る: to use up one's time
- {持|も}ち{時間|じかん}が{切|き}れる: to run out of time
- {持|も}ち{時間|じかん}{内|ない}に{収|おさ}める: to keep within the time allotted
- {各|かく}{持|も}ち{時間|じかん}{三時間|さんじかん}: three hours each

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {制限|せいげん}{時間|じかん}: time limit — an upper bound on how long something may take, not a personal allowance
- {時間切|じかんぎ}れ: running out of time — the state of having exhausted it
